flags: Receipts form one uniform list, with no separate `check` field in the tracking record, handoff report or review packet.
Maintained prompts and docs describe `verified_by` as the complete, explicit list.
If the Developer objects to the contract, the existing cannot-comply path returns the Intent to Shaping.
It is reused while the overlay digest is unchanged.
A catalog without the integrity fields labels every scenario `integrity-not-configured`.
Non-file selectors (rehearsal ids, root `.txt` fixtures, `scripts/check` files) stay existence-checked, and are labelled as such.
`Makefile` and `priv/kogen/verification_targets.yaml` stay byte-identical to main, because main's controller stops a Build whose catalog changed after admission.
Deterministic orchestration is proved offline, including through a complete fake-harness run.
Kogen's orchestration (controller, plan, receipts, tracking, reports, Jev plumbing, guards and catalog rules) is offline-only.
An Intent that edits a live test's owner file selects that test's target in the same Intent, because an edited live test that never runs is unverified.
it describes main's pre-Intent freeze instead of the controller this Intent ships
provider retries or timeouts are added to Kogen core or config
ledger dispositions are folded into the finding `dispositions`
Its evidence no longer requires `hook_receipt`, `checks` or `checks_before_resume`, and its prompts no longer tell the model that a Stop hook settles a Check.
Admission no longer requires a `check` target.
The no-context check-and-block mode and the `KOGEN_TRACKING_CONTEXT` path are gone.
Its base checks are skipped, and the report labels it `unproven-on-base`.

scenario.given: A controller verification cycle in which targets pass, fail, or leave processes behind.
scenario.then: Each receipt records the target, status, exit code, Candidate id, attempt token, context sha256, catalog sha256, cycle sequence, start and finish time, elapsed milliseconds, the output log path and sha256, and cleanup status. The controller runs each target in its own process group and, after exit, terminates any remaining group members. A target that leaves members that can't be reaped gets `cleanup: failed` and a failed receipt. Status comes from the exit code and cleanup only. A target-evidence manifest is snapshotted on pass *and* fail. Settlement rejects receipts with a mismatched binding, a rolled-back history or an altered log digest.
scenario.wrong_result: A receipt lacks its Candidate or catalog binding; owner-printed text changes the status; a leftover process is ignored; failed-target evidence is dropped
scenario.evidence: Focused tests with fake targets that pass, fail, spawn a lingering child, and emit a manifest. They assert every binding field of each receipt, that a target printing "PASS" with a nonzero exit gets a failed receipt, and that settlement rejects a receipt whose Candidate id or catalog digest was edited.

proof.paid_reason: offline-sufficient: controller runner with real child processes and a manifest-emitting fake target; no provider semantics are involved

then_clauses.c0: Each receipt records the target, status, exit code, Candidate id, attempt token, context sha256, catalog sha256, cycle sequence, start and finish time, elapsed milliseconds, the output log path and sha256, and cleanup status.
then_clauses.c1: The controller runs each target in its own process group and, after exit, terminates any remaining group members.
then_clauses.c2: A target that leaves members that can't be reaped gets `cleanup: failed` and a failed receipt.
then_clauses.c3: Status comes from the exit code and cleanup only.
then_clauses.c4: A target-evidence manifest is snapshotted on pass *and* fail.
then_clauses.c5: Settlement rejects receipts with a mismatched binding, a rolled-back history or an altered log digest.

scenario.given: A future Shaping session in this repository for an Intent that removes or replaces something Kogen's own Build process depends on while that Build is running.
scenario.when: The Shaping Controller reads `README.md`, as every Kogen Shaping session does.
scenario.then: Kogen's `README.md`, not the shared Shaping prompt, has a maintained section explaining that Kogen builds itself. A Build runs main's controller, the code loaded when `mix kogen.build` started, against a Candidate that is changing the same machinery. Removals therefore follow expand and contract, like a zero-downtime database migration. One Intent adds the new path, switches the new controller to it, and keeps the old path working for the running controller. The next Intent, built under the new controller, removes the old path. The section lists, with source locations as of this commit, what the running controller reads or runs from the Candidate during a Build: the catalog and its change rules; the Make target definitions; the admission catalog's integrity fields; the files and registrations `VerificationPolicy.preflight` requires; the Stop scripts and registrations (bootstrap only); the guarded-path check; and the approved package. It gives this Intent and its follow-up verification Intent as the worked example: the Stop scripts are kept for the v1 context and removed next, and the `live-native` split is done next through declared catalog changes. It tells Shaping to check each Intent that touches these inputs, and to split it when one Build can't both change the input and still settle, review and commit.
scenario.wrong_result: The guidance goes into `priv/kogen/prompts/shaping.md`, so it affects other projects; it names no concrete inputs; it describes main's pre-Intent freeze instead of the controller this Intent ships; it lives only in this Intent package
scenario.evidence: A README content test asserts the section heading, each listed input with its source location, and the worked example, and asserts that the shared Shaping prompt doesn't contain the Kogen-specific section.

proof.paid_reason: offline-sufficient: maintained README content asserted by a focused test; no provider semantics

scenario.given: A repository whose Makefile and catalog declare offline and provider-backed Make targets under any names. For example, an offline `test` target with no dependencies and no `check` target at all. The approved scenarios each list their targets in `verified_by`. (This is a fixture repository built under this Intent's controller. Kogen's own Makefile and catalog keep `check` unchanged in this Build, because main's controller runs it.)
scenario.when: `mix kogen.build` admits the Intent and verifies each Developer turn.
scenario.then: No target name is special; Make stays the only runner. Admission no longer requires a `check` target. The plan loader accepts a scenario's `verified_by` when all of these hold: it is a nonempty list of distinct catalog targets; it contains at least one `provider_backed: false` target and at most one `provider_backed: true` target, which must equal `proof.paid_target`; every listed target's `dependencies` are also listed; and the list follows catalog rank order. The Build runs exactly the union of the approved `verified_by` lists, in rank order, and never silently adds a target. Receipts form one uniform list, with no separate `check` field in the tracking record, handoff report or review packet. The Bash gate guard blocks `make <goal>` for every catalog target, not a hardcoded `check`/`live` pair. The catalog validator requires at least one offline target with no dependencies, instead of `check`. This repository's existing contracts (`[check]` and `[check, <paid>]`, including this Intent's own) still validate unchanged. Maintained prompts and docs describe `verified_by` as the complete, explicit list.
scenario.wrong_result: Admission still needs `make check`; `check` is still added implicitly or stored in its own field; a paid-only or dependency-incomplete `verified_by` is accepted; an unlisted target runs; the guard misses a renamed gate; existing approved contracts stop validating
scenario.evidence: Plan-loader and controller tests use a fixture repository whose catalog has an offline `test` target and no `check`. They include paid-only, missing dependency and out-of-order negative controls, a gate-guard control that blocks `make test` for the renamed gate, plus the current repository catalog and every Intent package under `approved/` as preservation controls.

proof.paid_reason: offline-sufficient: plan loading, target selection and guard naming are pure controller logic exercised through Kogen.Build with a fake harness; no provider semantics

scenario.given: A Candidate that changes, adds, deletes or renames files matching the admission catalog's `verification_surface` globs, including paths outside every scenario's `affected_paths`.
scenario.when: The controller prepares the handoff report and Review.
scenario.then: The controller computes a ledger from git (Candidate against base). For every changed surface path it records the status, the full diff and whether it is runner-class. It marks every target receipt that ran with changed runner-class files, and includes the catalog digest change. Added test-class files are left out; added runner-class files are included. The ledger goes into the handoff report and the review packet from bounded-reviewer-evidence, never to Jev. Each item's full diff is a controller-retained file under the attempt's verification directory. The packet carries one complete index entry per item (path, status, runner-class flag, diff stat, base and Candidate blob ids), plus a locator and sha256 for its full diff. It stays within the packet's 65,536-byte bound, and it never inlines a diff that would exceed it. The controller also runs base's test suite against the Candidate's implementation. Base's test files and runner go into the base workspace, with only the Candidate's implementation (non-surface) files overlaid. The result goes to Review as a packet summary with a log locator, a report and not a gate. The Reviewer must return exactly one disposition per ledger item, `justified: <scenario-id or finding-id>` or `weakening`, in a new `ledger` verdict field, kept separate from the existing finding `dispositions`. The field is required exactly when the packet carries a nonempty ledger. Without a ledger (for example when main's controller reviews this Build with the Candidate's `reviewer.md`), the verdict keeps today's exact keys. Both harnesses constrain the Reviewer's output with `Kogen.Harness.Verdict.schema/0` (Claude `--json-schema`, Codex `--output-schema`, both `additionalProperties: false`) and check exact keys in `Verdict.validate/1`. So the schema handed to a fresh Reviewer on either harness is chosen per launch: with a nonempty ledger it adds a required `ledger` array (one item per ledger path, `path` and `disposition`); without one it is byte-identical to today's schema. `Verdict.validate/1` and `Contract.verdict/4` accept `ledger` exactly when it was requested. A missing or extra disposition makes the Review malformed, through the existing malformed-verdict path. A `weakening` disposition opens a blocking finding that goes back to the same Developer as Review rework. If the Developer objects to the contract, the existing cannot-comply path returns the Intent to Shaping.
scenario.wrong_result: A weakened test outside `affected_paths` never reaches Review; the ledger or diff goes to Jev; the Reviewer can skip items; a `weakening` verdict doesn't block; the base-suite report acts as a gate or is missing; full diffs are inlined until the packet exceeds its bound; ledger dispositions are folded into the finding `dispositions`; `ledger` is demanded when no ledger was supplied, so main's controller rejects this Build's own verdict
scenario.evidence: Report and Review tests use a fixture Candidate that edits a test outside `affected_paths`, weakens a runner file and adds a test file. They assert the ledger contents, that the Jev request excludes them, the malformed verdict on a missing disposition, the blocking finding on `weakening`, the base-suite report, a packet within its bound for a ledger with large diffs (with locators and digests), and a verdict without `ledger` accepted when no ledger was supplied. The fake Claude and fake Codex Reviewers record the schema argument they were launched with: it contains `ledger` only with a ledger, and equals today's `Verdict.schema/0` bytes without one.

proof.paid_reason: offline-sufficient: ledger computation, verdict schema enforcement and routing are controller logic exercised with a fake Reviewer; no provider semantics

scenario.given: The Codex compatibility owner's live test, after this Intent deletes the Stop runner's no-context check-and-block mode.
scenario.when: The owner's live test runs through `live-native`.
scenario.then: The fixture no longer copies Stop scripts or relies on the deleted no-context Stop mode. Its evidence no longer requires `hook_receipt`, `checks` or `checks_before_resume`, and its prompts no longer tell the model that a Stop hook settles a Check. The PreToolUse blocked-gate, hostile discovery, interactive Shaping, Developer, exact-session resume (driven by the owner's fixed rework request) and scout-helper requirements remain. `cross-harness-adversarial-roles` already removed the scripted stand-in Reviewer turns, and this Intent doesn't bring a Reviewer back. The owner's turn budget, its one fresh-fixture retry after a timeout and its two-attempt evidence manifest are owned by `cross-harness-adversarial-roles`, which lands first. This Intent keeps them unchanged and doesn't add or remove any provider retry. Kogen core sees one target result.
scenario.wrong_result: The fixture still depends on Stop-hook receipts, so it fails once the no-context mode is gone; the Stop portion is removed by weakening the PreToolUse, discovery, resume or helper requirements; a stand-in Reviewer comes back; provider retries or timeouts are added to Kogen core or config; the owner's retry, budget or manifest from cross-harness are changed
scenario.evidence: Offline preparation tests assert the Stop-free fixture and the reduced evidence schema. The cross-harness assertions already in codex_compatibility_test (no stand-in Reviewer turn, the 240 s turn limit, one timed_out rerun, the two-attempt manifest) and the PreToolUse, discovery, resume and helper requirements stay and pass unedited. The paid `live-native` run exercises the Stop-free fixture with the real managed Codex runtime. `live-native` is still the unsplit target, because this Build can't change the catalog.

proof.paid_reason: provider-required: live-native; observation: the real managed Codex runtime completes the bounded compatibility run in a fixture without Stop hooks, with the PreToolUse gate denial, exact-session resume and scout helper intact; offline-limit: offline preparation tests cannot show that the real Codex CLI works without the Stop hooks; live-native is the only catalog target owning this file until the follow-up split

then_clauses.c1: Its evidence no longer requires `hook_receipt`, `checks` or `checks_before_resume`, and its prompts no longer tell the model that a Stop hook settles a Check.
then_clauses.c2: The PreToolUse blocked-gate, hostile discovery, interactive Shaping, Developer, exact-session resume (driven by the owner's fixed rework request) and scout-helper requirements remain.

scenario.given: An admission catalog that declares `verification_surface` (`tests` and `runner` globs), `focused_runner` (an argv template with `{paths}`) and `base_cache` (paths to copy). A contract whose scenarios carry the new `proof.base` field: `fail` for new or changed behaviour, `pass` for preservation.
scenario.when: The controller verifies each Developer turn.
scenario.then: After the targets pass, the controller itself runs each scenario's file selectors on the Candidate, using the admission `focused_runner`. A failure is a verification failure through the normal retry path. This replaces the existence-only check (`verification_plan.ex:94-103`). For `base: fail`, it also runs them against the base. At admission it builds a controller-owned workspace outside the repository: `git archive` of the admission commit plus copies of `base_cache`. It records the workspace's digest and re-checks it before each use; on a mismatch it rebuilds the workspace. The catalog loader rejects a `base_cache` entry inside the controller's volatile state (`.kogen/runtime`, `.kogen/build.lock`, `.kogen/codex`, `.codex/sessions`), so the base workspace never inherits the running Build's lock or runtime. Every focused run there uses the workspace's own `MIX_BUILD_PATH` and resolves `priv/` and prompts inside the workspace, never from the parent checkout or the controller's application directory. Each cycle it overlays only the Candidate's bytes for that scenario's selector files and changed test-class files, never runner-class or implementation files. It runs the admission `focused_runner` there with a time limit. The run must exit nonzero. Exit zero fails verification as "proof cannot detect the change". A timeout or infrastructure error is an error, never a red result. The red receipt records the base commit, overlay digest, exit code, log path and digest, and a `red_kind` label (`assertion` or `load`). It is reused while the overlay digest is unchanged. For `base: pass`, a selector that differs from base becomes a ledger item. The controller also runs base's bytes of that selector on the Candidate, and they must pass there. A contract without `proof.base` still validates. Its base checks are skipped, and the report labels it `unproven-on-base`. A catalog without the integrity fields labels every scenario `integrity-not-configured`. Non-file selectors (rehearsal ids, root `.txt` fixtures, `scripts/check` files) stay existence-checked, and are labelled as such.
scenario.wrong_result: An empty selector, `assert true`, or a scenario test hidden behind `:live` or a skip counts as proof; the red run uses the Candidate's runner or Candidate implementation files; a timeout counts as red; a tampered base workspace is reused; an edited preservation test passes without running base's bytes; legacy contracts are rejected instead of labelled
scenario.evidence: Controller tests use a fixture repository with a small ExUnit project and an admission catalog with the integrity fields. They cover: a real `fail` selector that is red on base and green on the Candidate; an empty selector and an `assert true` selector (both rejected); a `:live`-tagged selector (rejected); a runner file edited in the Candidate (the red run still uses base's runner); a tampered workspace digest; a `pass` selector weakened in the Candidate (base bytes fail on the Candidate); a legacy contract (labelled); a timeout (error, not red); removal of the temporary workspace; a `base_cache` entry naming `.kogen/build.lock` (rejected); and a base run whose `priv/` file differs from the parent checkout's, which must read the workspace's copy.

proof.paid_reason: offline-sufficient: the controller runs real focused tests in a fixture project against a real git-archive base; no provider semantics

then_clauses.c0: After the targets pass, the controller itself runs each scenario's file selectors on the Candidate, using the admission `focused_runner`.
then_clauses.c1: A failure is a verification failure through the normal retry path.
then_clauses.c2: This replaces the existence-only check (`verification_plan.ex:94-103`).
then_clauses.c3: For `base: fail`, it also runs them against the base.
then_clauses.c4: At admission it builds a controller-owned workspace outside the repository: `git archive` of the admission commit plus copies of `base_cache`.
then_clauses.c5: It records the workspace's digest and re-checks it before each use; on a mismatch it rebuilds the workspace.
then_clauses.c6: The catalog loader rejects a `base_cache` entry inside the controller's volatile state (`.kogen/runtime`, `.kogen/build.lock`, `.kogen/codex`, `.codex/sessions`), so the base workspace never inherits the running Build's lock or runtime.
then_clauses.c7: Every focused run there uses the workspace's own `MIX_BUILD_PATH` and resolves `priv/` and prompts inside the workspace, never from the parent checkout or the controller's application directory.
then_clauses.c8: Each cycle it overlays only the Candidate's bytes for that scenario's selector files and changed test-class files, never runner-class or implementation files.
then_clauses.c9: It runs the admission `focused_runner` there with a time limit.
then_clauses.c11: Exit zero fails verification as "proof cannot detect the change".
then_clauses.c12: A timeout or infrastructure error is an error, never a red result.
then_clauses.c13: The red receipt records the base commit, overlay digest, exit code, log path and digest, and a `red_kind` label (`assertion` or `load`).
then_clauses.c14: It is reused while the overlay digest is unchanged.
then_clauses.c15: For `base: pass`, a selector that differs from base becomes a ledger item.
then_clauses.c16: The controller also runs base's bytes of that selector on the Candidate, and they must pass there.
then_clauses.c18: Its base checks are skipped, and the report labels it `unproven-on-base`.
then_clauses.c19: A catalog without the integrity fields labels every scenario `integrity-not-configured`.
then_clauses.c20: Non-file selectors (rehearsal ids, root `.txt` fixtures, `scripts/check` files) stay existence-checked, and are labelled as such.

wrong_result_alternatives.w0: An empty selector, `assert true`, or a scenario test hidden behind `:live` or a skip counts as proof
wrong_result_alternatives.w1: the red run uses the Candidate's runner or Candidate implementation files
wrong_result_alternatives.w3: a tampered base workspace is reused
wrong_result_alternatives.w4: an edited preservation test passes without running base's bytes
wrong_result_alternatives.w5: legacy contracts are rejected instead of labelled

scenario.given: The Candidate after this Build, with the Stop scripts still registered in `priv/kogen/claude_code/settings.json` and `.codex/hooks.json`.
scenario.when: The Stop hook fires (a) with no context or a non-v1 context, as under the new controller or in the compatibility fixture, or (b) with a valid v1 unified `KOGEN_VERIFICATION_CONTEXT` from an older controller, as in the Build that installs this Intent.
scenario.then: (a) It prints `{"continue":true}`, runs no Make target, and writes no verification record, state, history or log. (b) It behaves exactly as today's unified protocol, so the older controller can settle, review and commit this Build automatically. `Makefile` and `priv/kogen/verification_targets.yaml` stay byte-identical to main, because main's controller stops a Build whose catalog changed after admission. `live-native` stays in the catalog unchanged. The target split belongs to the follow-up verification Intent. Main's `VerificationPolicy.preflight` still finds `.codex/hooks/check.sh`, `.codex/hooks/verification_policy.py` and the PreToolUse registration. The Candidate's own preflight requires only `.codex/hooks/verification_policy.py` and the PreToolUse registration, so the follow-up can delete the Stop scripts under this Intent's controller. Main's frozen catalog still runs every rehearsal inside `check`, so each rehearsal still observes its catalog trace identities, including `Kogen.Build.Verification.initialize` and `Kogen.Build.Verification.settle` through `test/kogen/verification_ownership_lifecycle_test.exs`, `Kogen.Build.Report.build` and `Kogen.Build.Contract.verdict` through `test/kogen/two_outer_resumptions_test.exs`, and `Kogen.Codex.Compatibility.prepare_fixture` through `test/kogen/codex_compatibility_preparation_test.exs`. Main's controller renders the Candidate's `priv/kogen/prompts/developer.md` at every Developer launch and outer resumption of this Build, and `priv/kogen/prompts/reviewer.md` at every Review. So the Candidate's prompts keep every placeholder main substitutes, describe verification truthfully for both routes (Stop settles when a v1 context is supplied, the controller otherwise), and request a verdict that main's `Kogen.Build.Contract.verdict/4` still accepts when no ledger is supplied. Every edited cataloged test gets only its `source_sha256` refreshed in `priv/kogen/test-reliability.yaml` through `scripts/check/refresh_test_reliability_sources.py`. Declarations, dispositions, controls and consumer witnesses are unchanged. The consumer modules keep their witness text (for example `defmodule Kogen.Check do`), and `--check` reports nothing. The no-context check-and-block mode and the `KOGEN_TRACKING_CONTEXT` path are gone. The Bash PreToolUse gate guard is still registered in both harnesses and still blocks `make check` and every selected target. The Developer and Reviewer prompts and the README describe controller-owned verification. They mention the Stop scripts only as bootstrap remnants that the follow-up Intent deletes.
scenario.wrong_result: Stop runs checks or blocks without a v1 context (a dual writer under the new controller); the v1 path is broken so this Build can't settle; the scripts or registrations are deleted in this Build; the Makefile or catalog changes (main's controller would stop the Build before Review, as in failed Build G8XQmw8OuNa-fPqe0TlQ0p35); the gate guard is removed; the Candidate's preflight still requires the Stop script, so the follow-up can't delete it; a rehearsal trace identity disappears, so `check` fails under main's frozen catalog; the Candidate prompts lose a placeholder or ask for a verdict key that main's controller rejects while it reviews this Build; the reliability ledger is regenerated, or a consumer witness is lost, instead of a hash-only refresh
scenario.evidence: A rewritten stop_hook test drives both cases with a real git fixture and counting fake targets. Harness contract and core integrity tests assert the hook sets for both harnesses, and the verification_policy tests keep the guard's denial controls and assert that the new preflight no longer needs the Stop script. The existing reliability-catalog test validates the refreshed ledger. The three catalog rehearsals (selected by id, and run inside `check` by `scripts/check/rehearsals.exs`) fail when a trace identity is no longer observed, and a prompt-rendering assertion in the harness contract test renders both prompts with main's placeholder set.

proof.paid_reason: offline-sufficient: stop_hook drives the real scripts in both context cases with a counting fake target; the inactive path prints the same {"continue":true} the real CLIs already accept

scenario.given: `verification_retries: 2` and a controller verification cycle that has failed.
scenario.when: The controller handles the failed cycle.
scenario.then: The controller resumes the exact Developer session with `resume_build_developer`. The resume names the failed target and its receipt and log paths. It counts against `verification_retries` and never the outer allowance. The third consecutive failure since the last pass marks verification exhausted and stops the Build, before Jev and Review and ahead of other routing. A Review or unfinished-work outer resumption starts a new verification context, and its handoff needs a fresh controller pass. The superseded-objection rule from bounded-reviewer-evidence keeps working on controller cycles: a confident Developer objection in an attempt whose settled controller verification passed after an earlier controller cycle of the same attempt failed reaches the review packet as a labelled advisory. Every other confident objection still stops with `cannot_comply` as before.
scenario.wrong_result: A verification failure consumes an outer resumption, launches a fresh Developer, reaches Review, or keeps retrying past the limit; an outer resumption reaches Review on the prior attempt's pass; the superseded-objection rule still reads Stop-written cycles, so under the new controller every stale objection stops the Build again
scenario.evidence: Fake-harness lifecycle tests count exact resumes, allowance counters, exhaustion precedence and the fresh context per outer attempt. The superseded-objection tests from bounded-reviewer-evidence run their three cases on controller-written cycles.

proof.paid_reason: offline-sufficient: fake-harness resume counting and exhaustion precedence through Kogen.Build; resume_build_developer itself is unchanged

scenario.given: A Shaper shaping an Intent in Kogen or another repository, with provider-backed targets in the catalog.
scenario.when: The Shaping Controller chooses each scenario's `verified_by`.
scenario.then: Kogen's shared Shaping prompt (`priv/kogen/prompts/shaping.md`) describes `verified_by` as the complete explicit list, with no implicit `check`. It says to select a provider-backed target only when the scenario claims a provider-only observable that offline proof can't establish. The fact that an existing live test exercises the changed path isn't a reason on its own. Deterministic orchestration is proved offline, including through a complete fake-harness run. The prompt replaces the current wording "Select targets by affected existing workflows ... even when their live test files are unchanged" and keeps the `provider-required` or `offline-sufficient` reason format. Kogen's own README gains a maintained "Choosing verification targets" section, read by Shaping as repository context. Kogen's orchestration (controller, plan, receipts, tracking, reports, Jev plumbing, guards and catalog rules) is offline-only. Prompt wording is offline-only unless the scenario claims a model-behaviour outcome. A paid target is reserved for native harness launch, resume or flags; native hook registration consumed by a real CLI; managed runtime upgrades; and parsing new provider output shapes. An Intent that edits a live test's owner file selects that test's target in the same Intent, because an edited live test that never runs is unverified. Otherwise an Intent selects at most one paid target, unless the Shaper explicitly accepts more, with the reason recorded in `questions.md`.
scenario.wrong_result: The prompt still steers toward live targets for unchanged live tests; still shows `[check]` as mandatory; drops the paid-reason format; the Kogen policy lives only in the transcript and not in maintained README text
scenario.evidence: Existing prompt-contract tests (scenario_contract, shape_task) assert the new selection wording, the removed "even when their live test files are unchanged" wording, and the README section headings and rules.

proof.paid_reason: offline-sufficient: maintained prompt and README content is asserted by prompt-contract tests; whether a future model follows it is not a claim of this scenario

state.then: Each receipt records the target, status, exit code, Candidate id, attempt token, context sha256, catalog sha256, cycle sequence, start and finish time, elapsed milliseconds, the output log path and sha256, and cleanup status. The controller runs each target in its own process group and, after exit, terminates any remaining group members. A target that leaves members that can't be reaped gets `cleanup: failed` and a failed receipt. Status comes from the exit code and cleanup only. A target-evidence manifest is snapshotted on pass *and* fail. Settlement rejects receipts with a mismatched binding, a rolled-back history or an altered log digest.

state.then: The controller computes a ledger from git (Candidate against base). For every changed surface path it records the status, the full diff and whether it is runner-class. It marks every target receipt that ran with changed runner-class files, and includes the catalog digest change. Added test-class files are left out; added runner-class files are included. The ledger goes into the handoff report and the review packet from bounded-reviewer-evidence, never to Jev. Each item's full diff is a controller-retained file under the attempt's verification directory. The packet carries one complete index entry per item (path, status, runner-class flag, diff stat, base and Candidate blob ids), plus a locator and sha256 for its full diff. It stays within the packet's 65,536-byte bound, and it never inlines a diff that would exceed it. The controller also runs base's test suite against the Candidate's implementation. Base's test files and runner go into the base workspace, with only the Candidate's implementation (non-surface) files overlaid. The result goes to Review as a packet summary with a log locator, a report and not a gate. The Reviewer must return exactly one disposition per ledger item, `justified: <scenario-id or finding-id>` or `weakening`, in a new `ledger` verdict field, kept separate from the existing finding `dispositions`. The field is required exactly when the packet carries a nonempty ledger. Without a ledger (for example when main's controller reviews this Build with the Candidate's `reviewer.md`), the verdict keeps today's exact keys. Both harnesses constrain the Reviewer's output with `Kogen.Harness.Verdict.schema/0` (Claude `--json-schema`, Codex `--output-schema`, both `additionalProperties: false`) and check exact keys in `Verdict.validate/1`. So the schema handed to a fresh Reviewer on either harness is chosen per launch: with a nonempty ledger it adds a required `ledger` array (one item per ledger path, `path` and `disposition`); without one it is byte-identical to today's schema. `Verdict.validate/1` and `Contract.verdict/4` accept `ledger` exactly when it was requested. A missing or extra disposition makes the Review malformed, through the existing malformed-verdict path. A `weakening` disposition opens a blocking finding that goes back to the same Developer as Review rework. If the Developer objects to the contract, the existing cannot-comply path returns the Intent to Shaping.

They assert the ledger contents, that the Jev request excludes them, the malformed verdict on a missing disposition, the blocking finding on `weakening`, the base-suite report, a packet within its bound for a ledger with large diffs (with locators and digests), and a verdict without `ledger` accepted when no ledger was supplied. The fake Claude and fake Codex Reviewers record the schema argument they were launched with: it contains `ledger` only with a ledger, and equals today's `Verdict.schema/0` bytes without one.

scenario.given: A Build started under the new controller, on any configured route (including the hybrid routes from cross-harness-adversarial-roles), whose Developer turn has just ended. The Stop registration still exists, but no v1 context is supplied.
scenario.when: The controller settles verification for that turn.
scenario.then: The parent controller, running the trusted code the Build started with, computes the Candidate id itself (a private-index git write-tree, refusing assume-unchanged and skip-worktree entries). It runs `make check`, then the selected targets in catalog order, as child processes outside the Developer process tree. It re-checks the Candidate id after each target; a mutation fails the cycle. It writes the only context, state and history files, and no Developer-launched process gets their paths or `KOGEN_VERIFICATION_CONTEXT`. It is also the only writer of the local Verification Record and its history (`Kogen.Check.record_path/0`, `Kogen.Check.history_path/0`). After each cycle it writes them in today's line format (candidate, status, target, exit_code, session_id, attempt_token, finished_at), and it archives and resets them only at each outer attempt, as today. The record's `target` field keeps the constant `check` as a format value for existing readers; it selects nothing. So the unedited live-reviewer-rework owner and its support files (`test/kogen/live_reviewer_rework_test.exs`, `test/support/live_reviewer_rework_fixture.ex`, `test/support/live_rework_audit.ex`) keep working, and this Intent leaves them byte-identical, because it doesn't run that target. This holds even when the controller itself inherited one: for example, a nested `mix kogen.build` started by a target under main's Stop runner inherits the outer v1 context. The new controller explicitly removes `KOGEN_VERIFICATION_CONTEXT` and `KOGEN_TRACKING_CONTEXT` from every Developer, Reviewer and target child environment. That way a nested fixture's Stop hook can't write to the outer Build's state. The Stop hook does nothing. Handoff, Jev and Review read only this controller settlement. A complete Build through the new controller shows a failed-then-passed controller verification across a resume of the same Developer session, followed by Review and commit.
scenario.wrong_result: The controller loads or executes verification code from the Candidate; reads success from a Candidate- or Developer-writable file; the Stop hook runs checks or blocks; the Developer gets a verification context, including one inherited from an outer Build's Stop runner; live_shape_to_build still asserts Stop-hook history; no process writes the local Verification Record and history any more (or they are archived on every inner cycle), so the unedited live-reviewer-rework audit fails in the next Build that runs it
scenario.evidence: A new controller verification test uses a fake harness to drive a turn end, controller-run check and targets, and forged Candidate state files that are ignored. A Candidate-planted module and script with the controller's verification names leave a sentinel only if loaded or run; the test asserts no sentinel, and that a counting Stop script run with no context runs no target and never blocks. It also plants an inherited outer `KOGEN_VERIFICATION_CONTEXT` and asserts that no launched child sees it and the outer state is untouched. It asserts that a failed-then-passed cycle pair leaves local Verification Record and history lines with the fields `Kogen.LiveReworkAudit` reads, and that the history is archived only when an outer attempt starts. The updated verification_ownership_lifecycle test runs a complete fake-harness Build through `Kogen.Build`, with real Make targets and a git fixture: a failed verification, a resume of the same session, a passed verification, Review and commit. `live_shape_to_build_test.exs` is updated to assert controller-owned failed-then-passed history for the same real Developer session. The value the Developer needs (`shape2build-k4q9z`) must now reach it through the controller's resume message, not through Stop output. The live test rsyncs the Candidate into its fixture and runs `mix kogen.build` there, which compiles and runs the Candidate's new controller (not main's, which only runs the outer Build). So the paid run observes the new route with a real Claude Code session.

state.then: The fixture no longer copies Stop scripts or relies on the deleted no-context Stop mode. Its evidence no longer requires `hook_receipt`, `checks` or `checks_before_resume`, and its prompts no longer tell the model that a Stop hook settles a Check. The PreToolUse blocked-gate, hostile discovery, interactive Shaping, Developer, exact-session resume (driven by the owner's fixed rework request) and scout-helper requirements remain. `cross-harness-adversarial-roles` already removed the scripted stand-in Reviewer turns, and this Intent doesn't bring a Reviewer back. The owner's turn budget, its one fresh-fixture retry after a timeout and its two-attempt evidence manifest are owned by `cross-harness-adversarial-roles`, which lands first. This Intent keeps them unchanged and doesn't add or remove any provider retry. Kogen core sees one target result.
state.evidence: Offline preparation tests assert the Stop-free fixture and the reduced evidence schema. The cross-harness assertions already in codex_compatibility_test (no stand-in Reviewer turn, the 240 s turn limit, one timed_out rerun, the two-attempt manifest) and the PreToolUse, discovery, resume and helper requirements stay and pass unedited. The paid `live-native` run exercises the Stop-free fixture with the real managed Codex runtime. `live-native` is still the unsplit target, because this Build can't change the catalog.

state.then: After the targets pass, the controller itself runs each scenario's file selectors on the Candidate, using the admission `focused_runner`. A failure is a verification failure through the normal retry path. This replaces the existence-only check (`verification_plan.ex:94-103`). For `base: fail`, it also runs them against the base. At admission it builds a controller-owned workspace outside the repository: `git archive` of the admission commit plus copies of `base_cache`. It records the workspace's digest and re-checks it before each use; on a mismatch it rebuilds the workspace. The catalog loader rejects a `base_cache` entry inside the controller's volatile state (`.kogen/runtime`, `.kogen/build.lock`, `.kogen/codex`, `.codex/sessions`), so the base workspace never inherits the running Build's lock or runtime. Every focused run there uses the workspace's own `MIX_BUILD_PATH` and resolves `priv/` and prompts inside the workspace, never from the parent checkout or the controller's application directory. Each cycle it overlays only the Candidate's bytes for that scenario's selector files and changed test-class files, never runner-class or implementation files. It runs the admission `focused_runner` there with a time limit. The run must exit nonzero. Exit zero fails verification as "proof cannot detect the change". A timeout or infrastructure error is an error, never a red result. The red receipt records the base commit, overlay digest, exit code, log path and digest, and a `red_kind` label (`assertion` or `load`). It is reused while the overlay digest is unchanged. For `base: pass`, a selector that differs from base becomes a ledger item. The controller also runs base's bytes of that selector on the Candidate, and they must pass there. A contract without `proof.base` still validates. Its base checks are skipped, and the report labels it `unproven-on-base`. A catalog without the integrity fields labels every scenario `integrity-not-configured`. Non-file selectors (rehearsal ids, root `.txt` fixtures, `scripts/check` files) stay existence-checked, and are labelled as such.
state.evidence: Controller tests use a fixture repository with a small ExUnit project and an admission catalog with the integrity fields. They cover: a real `fail` selector that is red on base and green on the Candidate; an empty selector and an `assert true` selector (both rejected); a `:live`-tagged selector (rejected); a runner file edited in the Candidate (the red run still uses base's runner); a tampered workspace digest; a `pass` selector weakened in the Candidate (base bytes fail on the Candidate); a legacy contract (labelled); a timeout (error, not red); removal of the temporary workspace; a `base_cache` entry naming `.kogen/build.lock` (rejected); and a base run whose `priv/` file differs from the parent checkout's, which must read the workspace's copy.

Kogen's orchestration (controller, plan, receipts, tracking, reports, Jev plumbing, guards and catalog rules) is offline-only. Prompt wording is offline-only unless the scenario claims a model-behaviour outcome. A paid target is reserved for native harness launch, resume or flags; native hook registration consumed by a real CLI; managed runtime upgrades; and parsing new provider output shapes. An Intent that edits a live test's owner file selects that test's target in the same Intent, because an edited live test that never runs is unverified. Otherwise an Intent selects at most one paid target, unless the Shaper explicitly accepts more, with the reason recorded in `questions.md`.

state.then: Each receipt records the target, status, exit code, Candidate id, attempt token, context sha256, catalog sha256, cycle sequence, start and finish time, elapsed milliseconds, the output log path and sha256, and cleanup status. The controller runs each target in its own process group and, after exit, terminates any remaining group members. A target that leaves members that can't be reaped gets `cleanup: failed` and a failed receipt. Status comes from the exit code and cleanup only. A target-evidence manifest is snapshotted on pass *and* fail. Settlement rejects receipts with a mismatched binding, a rolled-back history or an altered log digest.

state.then: The controller computes a ledger from git (Candidate against base). For every changed surface path it records the status, the full diff and whether it is runner-class. It marks every target receipt that ran with changed runner-class files, and includes the catalog digest change. Added test-class files are left out; added runner-class files are included. The ledger goes into the handoff report and the review packet from bounded-reviewer-evidence, never to Jev. Each item's full diff is a controller-retained file under the attempt's verification directory. The packet carries one complete index entry per item (path, status, runner-class flag, diff stat, base and Candidate blob ids), plus a locator and sha256 for its full diff. It stays within the packet's 65,536-byte bound, and it never inlines a diff that would exceed it. The controller also runs base's test suite against the Candidate's implementation. Base's test files and runner go into the base workspace, with only the Candidate's implementation (non-surface) files overlaid. The result goes to Review as a packet summary with a log locator, a report and not a gate. The Reviewer must return exactly one disposition per ledger item, `justified: <scenario-id or finding-id>` or `weakening`, in a new `ledger` verdict field, kept separate from the existing finding `dispositions`. The field is required exactly when the packet carries a nonempty ledger. Without a ledger (for example when main's controller reviews this Build with the Candidate's `reviewer.md`), the verdict keeps today's exact keys. Both harnesses constrain the Reviewer's output with `Kogen.Harness.Verdict.schema/0` (Claude `--json-schema`, Codex `--output-schema`, both `additionalProperties: false`) and check exact keys in `Verdict.validate/1`. So the schema handed to a fresh Reviewer on either harness is chosen per launch: with a nonempty ledger it adds a required `ledger` array (one item per ledger path, `path` and `disposition`); without one it is byte-identical to today's schema. `Verdict.validate/1` and `Contract.verdict/4` accept `ledger` exactly when it was requested. A missing or extra disposition makes the Review malformed, through the existing malformed-verdict path. A `weakening` disposition opens a blocking finding that goes back to the same Developer as Review rework. If the Developer objects to the contract, the existing cannot-comply path returns the Intent to Shaping.

state.then: After the targets pass, the controller itself runs each scenario's file selectors on the Candidate, using the admission `focused_runner`. A failure is a verification failure through the normal retry path. This replaces the existence-only check (`verification_plan.ex:94-103`). For `base: fail`, it also runs them against the base. At admission it builds a controller-owned workspace outside the repository: `git archive` of the admission commit plus copies of `base_cache`. It records the workspace's digest and re-checks it before each use; on a mismatch it rebuilds the workspace. The catalog loader rejects a `base_cache` entry inside the controller's volatile state (`.kogen/runtime`, `.kogen/build.lock`, `.kogen/codex`, `.codex/sessions`), so the base workspace never inherits the running Build's lock or runtime. Every focused run there uses the workspace's own `MIX_BUILD_PATH` and resolves `priv/` and prompts inside the workspace, never from the parent checkout or the controller's application directory. Each cycle it overlays only the Candidate's bytes for that scenario's selector files and changed test-class files, never runner-class or implementation files. It runs the admission `focused_runner` there with a time limit. The run must exit nonzero. Exit zero fails verification as "proof cannot detect the change". A timeout or infrastructure error is an error, never a red result. The red receipt records the base commit, overlay digest, exit code, log path and digest, and a `red_kind` label (`assertion` or `load`). It is reused while the overlay digest is unchanged. For `base: pass`, a selector that differs from base becomes a ledger item. The controller also runs base's bytes of that selector on the Candidate, and they must pass there. A contract without `proof.base` still validates. Its base checks are skipped, and the report labels it `unproven-on-base`. A catalog without the integrity fields labels every scenario `integrity-not-configured`. Non-file selectors (rehearsal ids, root `.txt` fixtures, `scripts/check` files) stay existence-checked, and are labelled as such.

After each cycle it writes them in today's line format (candidate, status, target, exit_code, session_id, attempt_token, finished_at), and it archives and resets them only at each outer attempt, as today. state.then: The controller computes a ledger from git (Candidate against base). For every changed surface path it records the status, the full diff and whether it is runner-class. It marks every target receipt that ran with changed runner-class files, and includes the catalog digest change. Added test-class files are left out; added runner-class files are included. The ledger goes into the handoff report and the review packet from bounded-reviewer-evidence, never to Jev. Each item's full diff is a controller-retained file under the attempt's verification directory. The packet carries one complete index entry per item (path, status, runner-class flag, diff stat, base and Candidate blob ids), plus a locator and sha256 for its full diff. It stays within the packet's 65,536-byte bound, and it never inlines a diff that would exceed it. The controller also runs base's test suite against the Candidate's implementation. Base's test files and runner go into the base workspace, with only the Candidate's implementation (non-surface) files overlaid. The result goes to Review as a packet summary with a log locator, a report and not a gate. The Reviewer must return exactly one disposition per ledger item, `justified: <scenario-id or finding-id>` or `weakening`, in a new `ledger` verdict field, kept separate from the existing finding `dispositions`. The field is required exactly when the packet carries a nonempty ledger. Without a ledger (for example when main's controller reviews this Build with the Candidate's `reviewer.md`), the verdict keeps today's exact keys. Both harnesses constrain the Reviewer's output with `Kogen.Harness.Verdict.schema/0` (Claude `--json-schema`, Codex `--output-schema`, both `additionalProperties: false`) and check exact keys in `Verdict.validate/1`. So the schema handed to a fresh Reviewer on either harness is chosen per launch: with a nonempty ledger it adds a required `ledger` array (one item per ledger path, `path` and `disposition`); without one it is byte-identical to today's schema. `Verdict.validate/1` and `Contract.verdict/4` accept `ledger` exactly when it was requested. A missing or extra disposition makes the Review malformed, through the existing malformed-verdict path. A `weakening` disposition opens a blocking finding that goes back to the same Developer as Review rework. If the Developer objects to the contract, the existing cannot-comply path returns the Intent to Shaping.

The fake Claude and fake Codex Reviewers record the schema argument they were launched with: it contains `ledger` only with a ledger, and equals today's `Verdict.schema/0` bytes without one.

state.then: After the targets pass, the controller itself runs each scenario's file selectors on the Candidate, using the admission `focused_runner`. A failure is a verification failure through the normal retry path. This replaces the existence-only check (`verification_plan.ex:94-103`). For `base: fail`, it also runs them against the base. At admission it builds a controller-owned workspace outside the repository: `git archive` of the admission commit plus copies of `base_cache`. It records the workspace's digest and re-checks it before each use; on a mismatch it rebuilds the workspace. The catalog loader rejects a `base_cache` entry inside the controller's volatile state (`.kogen/runtime`, `.kogen/build.lock`, `.kogen/codex`, `.codex/sessions`), so the base workspace never inherits the running Build's lock or runtime. Every focused run there uses the workspace's own `MIX_BUILD_PATH` and resolves `priv/` and prompts inside the workspace, never from the parent checkout or the controller's application directory. Each cycle it overlays only the Candidate's bytes for that scenario's selector files and changed test-class files, never runner-class or implementation files. It runs the admission `focused_runner` there with a time limit. The run must exit nonzero. Exit zero fails verification as "proof cannot detect the change". A timeout or infrastructure error is an error, never a red result. The red receipt records the base commit, overlay digest, exit code, log path and digest, and a `red_kind` label (`assertion` or `load`). It is reused while the overlay digest is unchanged. For `base: pass`, a selector that differs from base becomes a ledger item. The controller also runs base's bytes of that selector on the Candidate, and they must pass there. A contract without `proof.base` still validates. Its base checks are skipped, and the report labels it `unproven-on-base`. A catalog without the integrity fields labels every scenario `integrity-not-configured`. Non-file selectors (rehearsal ids, root `.txt` fixtures, `scripts/check` files) stay existence-checked, and are labelled as such.

state.then: The parent controller, running the trusted code the Build started with, computes the Candidate id itself (a private-index git write-tree, refusing assume-unchanged and skip-worktree entries). It runs `make check`, then the selected targets in catalog order, as child processes outside the Developer process tree. It re-checks the Candidate id after each target; a mutation fails the cycle. It writes the only context, state and history files, and no Developer-launched process gets their paths or `KOGEN_VERIFICATION_CONTEXT`. It is also the only writer of the local Verification Record and its history (`Kogen.Check.record_path/0`, `Kogen.Check.history_path/0`). After each cycle it writes them in today's line format (candidate, status, target, exit_code, session_id, attempt_token, finished_at), and it archives and resets them only at each outer attempt, as today. The record's `target` field keeps the constant `check` as a format value for existing readers; it selects nothing. So the unedited live-reviewer-rework owner and its support files (`test/kogen/live_reviewer_rework_test.exs`, `test/support/live_reviewer_rework_fixture.ex`, `test/support/live_rework_audit.ex`) keep working, and this Intent leaves them byte-identical, because it doesn't run that target. This holds even when the controller itself inherited one: for example, a nested `mix kogen.build` started by a target under main's Stop runner inherits the outer v1 context. The new controller explicitly removes `KOGEN_VERIFICATION_CONTEXT` and `KOGEN_TRACKING_CONTEXT` from every Developer, Reviewer and target child environment. That way a nested fixture's Stop hook can't write to the outer Build's state. The Stop hook does nothing. Handoff, Jev and Review read only this controller settlement. A complete Build through the new controller shows a failed-then-passed controller verification across a resume of the same Developer session, followed by Review and commit.

state.then: The controller computes a ledger from git (Candidate against base). For every changed surface path it records the status, the full diff and whether it is runner-class. It marks every target receipt that ran with changed runner-class files, and includes the catalog digest change. Added test-class files are left out; added runner-class files are included. The ledger goes into the handoff report and the review packet from bounded-reviewer-evidence, never to Jev. Each item's full diff is a controller-retained file under the attempt's verification directory. The packet carries one complete index entry per item (path, status, runner-class flag, diff stat, base and Candidate blob ids), plus a locator and sha256 for its full diff. It stays within the packet's 65,536-byte bound, and it never inlines a diff that would exceed it. The controller also runs base's test suite against the Candidate's implementation. Base's test files and runner go into the base workspace, with only the Candidate's implementation (non-surface) files overlaid. The result goes to Review as a packet summary with a log locator, a report and not a gate. The Reviewer must return exactly one disposition per ledger item, `justified: <scenario-id or finding-id>` or `weakening`, in a new `ledger` verdict field, kept separate from the existing finding `dispositions`. The field is required exactly when the packet carries a nonempty ledger. Without a ledger (for example when main's controller reviews this Build with the Candidate's `reviewer.md`), the verdict keeps today's exact keys. Both harnesses constrain the Reviewer's output with `Kogen.Harness.Verdict.schema/0` (Claude `--json-schema`, Codex `--output-schema`, both `additionalProperties: false`) and check exact keys in `Verdict.validate/1`. So the schema handed to a fresh Reviewer on either harness is chosen per launch: with a nonempty ledger it adds a required `ledger` array (one item per ledger path, `path` and `disposition`); without one it is byte-identical to today's schema. `Verdict.validate/1` and `Contract.verdict/4` accept `ledger` exactly when it was requested. A missing or extra disposition makes the Review malformed, through the existing malformed-verdict path. A `weakening` disposition opens a blocking finding that goes back to the same Developer as Review rework. If the Developer objects to the contract, the existing cannot-comply path returns the Intent to Shaping.

state.then: After the targets pass, the controller itself runs each scenario's file selectors on the Candidate, using the admission `focused_runner`. A failure is a verification failure through the normal retry path. This replaces the existence-only check (`verification_plan.ex:94-103`). For `base: fail`, it also runs them against the base. At admission it builds a controller-owned workspace outside the repository: `git archive` of the admission commit plus copies of `base_cache`. It records the workspace's digest and re-checks it before each use; on a mismatch it rebuilds the workspace. The catalog loader rejects a `base_cache` entry inside the controller's volatile state (`.kogen/runtime`, `.kogen/build.lock`, `.kogen/codex`, `.codex/sessions`), so the base workspace never inherits the running Build's lock or runtime. Every focused run there uses the workspace's own `MIX_BUILD_PATH` and resolves `priv/` and prompts inside the workspace, never from the parent checkout or the controller's application directory. Each cycle it overlays only the Candidate's bytes for that scenario's selector files and changed test-class files, never runner-class or implementation files. It runs the admission `focused_runner` there with a time limit. The run must exit nonzero. Exit zero fails verification as "proof cannot detect the change". A timeout or infrastructure error is an error, never a red result. The red receipt records the base commit, overlay digest, exit code, log path and digest, and a `red_kind` label (`assertion` or `load`). It is reused while the overlay digest is unchanged. For `base: pass`, a selector that differs from base becomes a ledger item. The controller also runs base's bytes of that selector on the Candidate, and they must pass there. A contract without `proof.base` still validates. Its base checks are skipped, and the report labels it `unproven-on-base`. A catalog without the integrity fields labels every scenario `integrity-not-configured`. Non-file selectors (rehearsal ids, root `.txt` fixtures, `scripts/check` files) stay existence-checked, and are labelled as such.

state.then: The controller computes a ledger from git (Candidate against base). For every changed surface path it records the status, the full diff and whether it is runner-class. It marks every target receipt that ran with changed runner-class files, and includes the catalog digest change. Added test-class files are left out; added runner-class files are included. The ledger goes into the handoff report and the review packet from bounded-reviewer-evidence, never to Jev. Each item's full diff is a controller-retained file under the attempt's verification directory. The packet carries one complete index entry per item (path, status, runner-class flag, diff stat, base and Candidate blob ids), plus a locator and sha256 for its full diff. It stays within the packet's 65,536-byte bound, and it never inlines a diff that would exceed it. The controller also runs base's test suite against the Candidate's implementation. Base's test files and runner go into the base workspace, with only the Candidate's implementation (non-surface) files overlaid. The result goes to Review as a packet summary with a log locator, a report and not a gate. The Reviewer must return exactly one disposition per ledger item, `justified: <scenario-id or finding-id>` or `weakening`, in a new `ledger` verdict field, kept separate from the existing finding `dispositions`. The field is required exactly when the packet carries a nonempty ledger. Without a ledger (for example when main's controller reviews this Build with the Candidate's `reviewer.md`), the verdict keeps today's exact keys. Both harnesses constrain the Reviewer's output with `Kogen.Harness.Verdict.schema/0` (Claude `--json-schema`, Codex `--output-schema`, both `additionalProperties: false`) and check exact keys in `Verdict.validate/1`. So the schema handed to a fresh Reviewer on either harness is chosen per launch: with a nonempty ledger it adds a required `ledger` array (one item per ledger path, `path` and `disposition`); without one it is byte-identical to today's schema. `Verdict.validate/1` and `Contract.verdict/4` accept `ledger` exactly when it was requested. A missing or extra disposition makes the Review malformed, through the existing malformed-verdict path. A `weakening` disposition opens a blocking finding that goes back to the same Developer as Review rework. If the Developer objects to the contract, the existing cannot-comply path returns the Intent to Shaping.

state.then: After the targets pass, the controller itself runs each scenario's file selectors on the Candidate, using the admission `focused_runner`. A failure is a verification failure through the normal retry path. This replaces the existence-only check (`verification_plan.ex:94-103`). For `base: fail`, it also runs them against the base. At admission it builds a controller-owned workspace outside the repository: `git archive` of the admission commit plus copies of `base_cache`. It records the workspace's digest and re-checks it before each use; on a mismatch it rebuilds the workspace. The catalog loader rejects a `base_cache` entry inside the controller's volatile state (`.kogen/runtime`, `.kogen/build.lock`, `.kogen/codex`, `.codex/sessions`), so the base workspace never inherits the running Build's lock or runtime. Every focused run there uses the workspace's own `MIX_BUILD_PATH` and resolves `priv/` and prompts inside the workspace, never from the parent checkout or the controller's application directory. Each cycle it overlays only the Candidate's bytes for that scenario's selector files and changed test-class files, never runner-class or implementation files. It runs the admission `focused_runner` there with a time limit. The run must exit nonzero. Exit zero fails verification as "proof cannot detect the change". A timeout or infrastructure error is an error, never a red result. The red receipt records the base commit, overlay digest, exit code, log path and digest, and a `red_kind` label (`assertion` or `load`). It is reused while the overlay digest is unchanged. For `base: pass`, a selector that differs from base becomes a ledger item. The controller also runs base's bytes of that selector on the Candidate, and they must pass there. A contract without `proof.base` still validates. Its base checks are skipped, and the report labels it `unproven-on-base`. A catalog without the integrity fields labels every scenario `integrity-not-configured`. Non-file selectors (rehearsal ids, root `.txt` fixtures, `scripts/check` files) stay existence-checked, and are labelled as such.

state.then: After the targets pass, the controller itself runs each scenario's file selectors on the Candidate, using the admission `focused_runner`. A failure is a verification failure through the normal retry path. This replaces the existence-only check (`verification_plan.ex:94-103`). For `base: fail`, it also runs them against the base. At admission it builds a controller-owned workspace outside the repository: `git archive` of the admission commit plus copies of `base_cache`. It records the workspace's digest and re-checks it before each use; on a mismatch it rebuilds the workspace. The catalog loader rejects a `base_cache` entry inside the controller's volatile state (`.kogen/runtime`, `.kogen/build.lock`, `.kogen/codex`, `.codex/sessions`), so the base workspace never inherits the running Build's lock or runtime. Every focused run there uses the workspace's own `MIX_BUILD_PATH` and resolves `priv/` and prompts inside the workspace, never from the parent checkout or the controller's application directory. Each cycle it overlays only the Candidate's bytes for that scenario's selector files and changed test-class files, never runner-class or implementation files. It runs the admission `focused_runner` there with a time limit. The run must exit nonzero. Exit zero fails verification as "proof cannot detect the change". A timeout or infrastructure error is an error, never a red result. The red receipt records the base commit, overlay digest, exit code, log path and digest, and a `red_kind` label (`assertion` or `load`). It is reused while the overlay digest is unchanged. For `base: pass`, a selector that differs from base becomes a ledger item. The controller also runs base's bytes of that selector on the Candidate, and they must pass there. A contract without `proof.base` still validates. Its base checks are skipped, and the report labels it `unproven-on-base`. A catalog without the integrity fields labels every scenario `integrity-not-configured`. Non-file selectors (rehearsal ids, root `.txt` fixtures, `scripts/check` files) stay existence-checked, and are labelled as such.

state.then: The controller computes a ledger from git (Candidate against base). For every changed surface path it records the status, the full diff and whether it is runner-class. It marks every target receipt that ran with changed runner-class files, and includes the catalog digest change. Added test-class files are left out; added runner-class files are included. The ledger goes into the handoff report and the review packet from bounded-reviewer-evidence, never to Jev. Each item's full diff is a controller-retained file under the attempt's verification directory. The packet carries one complete index entry per item (path, status, runner-class flag, diff stat, base and Candidate blob ids), plus a locator and sha256 for its full diff. It stays within the packet's 65,536-byte bound, and it never inlines a diff that would exceed it. The controller also runs base's test suite against the Candidate's implementation. Base's test files and runner go into the base workspace, with only the Candidate's implementation (non-surface) files overlaid. The result goes to Review as a packet summary with a log locator, a report and not a gate. The Reviewer must return exactly one disposition per ledger item, `justified: <scenario-id or finding-id>` or `weakening`, in a new `ledger` verdict field, kept separate from the existing finding `dispositions`. The field is required exactly when the packet carries a nonempty ledger. Without a ledger (for example when main's controller reviews this Build with the Candidate's `reviewer.md`), the verdict keeps today's exact keys. Both harnesses constrain the Reviewer's output with `Kogen.Harness.Verdict.schema/0` (Claude `--json-schema`, Codex `--output-schema`, both `additionalProperties: false`) and check exact keys in `Verdict.validate/1`. So the schema handed to a fresh Reviewer on either harness is chosen per launch: with a nonempty ledger it adds a required `ledger` array (one item per ledger path, `path` and `disposition`); without one it is byte-identical to today's schema. `Verdict.validate/1` and `Contract.verdict/4` accept `ledger` exactly when it was requested. A missing or extra disposition makes the Review malformed, through the existing malformed-verdict path. A `weakening` disposition opens a blocking finding that goes back to the same Developer as Review rework. If the Developer objects to the contract, the existing cannot-comply path returns the Intent to Shaping.

The fake Claude and fake Codex Reviewers record the schema argument they were launched with: it contains `ledger` only with a ledger, and equals today's `Verdict.schema/0` bytes without one.

state.then: The parent controller, running the trusted code the Build started with, computes the Candidate id itself (a private-index git write-tree, refusing assume-unchanged and skip-worktree entries). It runs `make check`, then the selected targets in catalog order, as child processes outside the Developer process tree. It re-checks the Candidate id after each target; a mutation fails the cycle. It writes the only context, state and history files, and no Developer-launched process gets their paths or `KOGEN_VERIFICATION_CONTEXT`. It is also the only writer of the local Verification Record and its history (`Kogen.Check.record_path/0`, `Kogen.Check.history_path/0`). After each cycle it writes them in today's line format (candidate, status, target, exit_code, session_id, attempt_token, finished_at), and it archives and resets them only at each outer attempt, as today. The record's `target` field keeps the constant `check` as a format value for existing readers; it selects nothing. So the unedited live-reviewer-rework owner and its support files (`test/kogen/live_reviewer_rework_test.exs`, `test/support/live_reviewer_rework_fixture.ex`, `test/support/live_rework_audit.ex`) keep working, and this Intent leaves them byte-identical, because it doesn't run that target. This holds even when the controller itself inherited one: for example, a nested `mix kogen.build` started by a target under main's Stop runner inherits the outer v1 context. The new controller explicitly removes `KOGEN_VERIFICATION_CONTEXT` and `KOGEN_TRACKING_CONTEXT` from every Developer, Reviewer and target child environment. That way a nested fixture's Stop hook can't write to the outer Build's state. The Stop hook does nothing. Handoff, Jev and Review read only this controller settlement. A complete Build through the new controller shows a failed-then-passed controller verification across a resume of the same Developer session, followed by Review and commit.

It also plants an inherited outer `KOGEN_VERIFICATION_CONTEXT` and asserts that no launched child sees it and the outer state is untouched. It asserts that a failed-then-passed cycle pair leaves local Verification Record and history lines with the fields `Kogen.LiveReworkAudit` reads, and that the history is archived only when an outer attempt starts. The updated verification_ownership_lifecycle test runs a complete fake-harness Build through `Kogen.Build`, with real Make targets and a git fixture: a failed verification, a resume of the same session, a passed verification, Review and commit. `live_shape_to_build_test.exs` is updated to assert controller-owned failed-then-passed history for the same real Developer session. The value the Developer needs (`shape2build-k4q9z`) must now reach it through the controller's resume message, not through Stop output. The live test rsyncs the Candidate into its fixture and runs `mix kogen.build` there, which compiles and runs the Candidate's new controller (not main's, which only runs the outer Build). So the paid run observes the new route with a real Claude Code session.

state.then: The catalog is no longer byte-frozen after admission. At admission, `verified_by` may name a declared added target. It is rejected when it names an undeclared unknown target, or when `add` names a target that already exists. Each cycle, the controller reads the Candidate's catalog and Makefile only as data; it never loads Candidate code. Every selected target must exist in both. Every added target must meet every catalog rule (unique rank, dependencies, owner, and a rehearsal when provider-backed). A scenario that selects an added provider-backed target lists that target's rehearsal test as a file selector, so `controller-runs-proof-selectors` covers it. Removing, renaming or editing unselected targets needs no declaration; it appears in the verification-surface ledger. A missing or invalid selected target is a verification failure that resumes the same Developer. It doesn't stop the Build. The trust anchor for each rule is the admission catalog, never the Candidate's.

state.then: The controller computes a ledger from git (Candidate against base). For every changed surface path it records the status, the full diff and whether it is runner-class. It marks every target receipt that ran with changed runner-class files, and includes the catalog digest change. Added test-class files are left out; added runner-class files are included. The ledger goes into the handoff report and the review packet from bounded-reviewer-evidence, never to Jev. Each item's full diff is a controller-retained file under the attempt's verification directory. The packet carries one complete index entry per item (path, status, runner-class flag, diff stat, base and Candidate blob ids), plus a locator and sha256 for its full diff. It stays within the packet's 65,536-byte bound, and it never inlines a diff that would exceed it. The controller also runs base's test suite against the Candidate's implementation. Base's test files and runner go into the base workspace, with only the Candidate's implementation (non-surface) files overlaid. The result goes to Review as a packet summary with a log locator, a report and not a gate. The Reviewer must return exactly one disposition per ledger item, `justified: <scenario-id or finding-id>` or `weakening`, in a new `ledger` verdict field, kept separate from the existing finding `dispositions`. The field is required exactly when the packet carries a nonempty ledger. Without a ledger (for example when main's controller reviews this Build with the Candidate's `reviewer.md`), the verdict keeps today's exact keys. Both harnesses constrain the Reviewer's output with `Kogen.Harness.Verdict.schema/0` (Claude `--json-schema`, Codex `--output-schema`, both `additionalProperties: false`) and check exact keys in `Verdict.validate/1`. So the schema handed to a fresh Reviewer on either harness is chosen per launch: with a nonempty ledger it adds a required `ledger` array (one item per ledger path, `path` and `disposition`); without one it is byte-identical to today's schema. `Verdict.validate/1` and `Contract.verdict/4` accept `ledger` exactly when it was requested. A missing or extra disposition makes the Review malformed, through the existing malformed-verdict path. A `weakening` disposition opens a blocking finding that goes back to the same Developer as Review rework. If the Developer objects to the contract, the existing cannot-comply path returns the Intent to Shaping.

state.then: The parent controller, running the trusted code the Build started with, computes the Candidate id itself (a private-index git write-tree, refusing assume-unchanged and skip-worktree entries). It runs `make check`, then the selected targets in catalog order, as child processes outside the Developer process tree. It re-checks the Candidate id after each target; a mutation fails the cycle. It writes the only context, state and history files, and no Developer-launched process gets their paths or `KOGEN_VERIFICATION_CONTEXT`. It is also the only writer of the local Verification Record and its history (`Kogen.Check.record_path/0`, `Kogen.Check.history_path/0`). After each cycle it writes them in today's line format (candidate, status, target, exit_code, session_id, attempt_token, finished_at), and it archives and resets them only at each outer attempt, as today. The record's `target` field keeps the constant `check` as a format value for existing readers; it selects nothing. So the unedited live-reviewer-rework owner and its support files (`test/kogen/live_reviewer_rework_test.exs`, `test/support/live_reviewer_rework_fixture.ex`, `test/support/live_rework_audit.ex`) keep working, and this Intent leaves them byte-identical, because it doesn't run that target. This holds even when the controller itself inherited one: for example, a nested `mix kogen.build` started by a target under main's Stop runner inherits the outer v1 context. The new controller explicitly removes `KOGEN_VERIFICATION_CONTEXT` and `KOGEN_TRACKING_CONTEXT` from every Developer, Reviewer and target child environment. That way a nested fixture's Stop hook can't write to the outer Build's state. The Stop hook does nothing. Handoff, Jev and Review read only this controller settlement. A complete Build through the new controller shows a failed-then-passed controller verification across a resume of the same Developer session, followed by Review and commit.
