state.then: The controller computes a ledger from git (Candidate against base). For every changed surface path it records the status, the full diff and whether it is runner-class. It marks every target receipt that ran with changed runner-class files, and includes the catalog digest change. Added test-class files are left out; added runner-class files are included. The ledger goes into the handoff report and the review packet from bounded-reviewer-evidence, never to Jev. Each item's full diff is a controller-retained file under the attempt's verification directory. The packet carries one complete index entry per item (path, status, runner-class flag, diff stat, base and Candidate blob ids), plus a locator and sha256 for its full diff. It stays within the packet's 65,536-byte bound, and it never inlines a diff that would exceed it. The controller also runs base's test suite against the Candidate's implementation. Base's test files and runner go into the base workspace, with only the Candidate's implementation (non-surface) files overlaid. The result goes to Review as a packet summary with a log locator, a report and not a gate. The Reviewer must return exactly one disposition per ledger item, `justified: <scenario-id or finding-id>` or `weakening`, in a new `ledger` verdict field, kept separate from the existing finding `dispositions`. The field is required exactly when the packet carries a nonempty ledger. Without a ledger (for example when main's controller reviews this Build with the Candidate's `reviewer.md`), the verdict keeps today's exact keys. Both harnesses constrain the Reviewer's output with `Kogen.Harness.Verdict.schema/0` (Claude `--json-schema`, Codex `--output-schema`, both `additionalProperties: false`) and check exact keys in `Verdict.validate/1`. So the schema handed to a fresh Reviewer on either harness is chosen per launch: with a nonempty ledger it adds a required `ledger` array (one item per ledger path, `path` and `disposition`); without one it is byte-identical to today's schema. `Verdict.validate/1` and `Contract.verdict/4` accept `ledger` exactly when it was requested. A missing or extra disposition makes the Review malformed, through the existing malformed-verdict path. A `weakening` disposition opens a blocking finding that goes back to the same Developer as Review rework. If the Developer objects to the contract, the existing cannot-comply path returns the Intent to Shaping.

The fake Claude and fake Codex Reviewers record the schema argument they were launched with: it contains `ledger` only with a ledger, and equals today's `Verdict.schema/0` bytes without one.

state.then: (a) It prints `{"continue":true}`, runs no Make target, and writes no verification record, state, history or log. (b) It behaves exactly as today's unified protocol, so the older controller can settle, review and commit this Build automatically. `Makefile` and `priv/kogen/verification_targets.yaml` stay byte-identical to main, because main's controller stops a Build whose catalog changed after admission. `live-native` stays in the catalog unchanged. The target split belongs to the follow-up verification Intent. Main's `VerificationPolicy.preflight` still finds `.codex/hooks/check.sh`, `.codex/hooks/verification_policy.py` and the PreToolUse registration. The Candidate's own preflight requires only `.codex/hooks/verification_policy.py` and the PreToolUse registration, so the follow-up can delete the Stop scripts under this Intent's controller. Main's frozen catalog still runs every rehearsal inside `check`, so each rehearsal still observes its catalog trace identities, including `Kogen.Build.Verification.initialize` and `Kogen.Build.Verification.settle` through `test/kogen/verification_ownership_lifecycle_test.exs`, `Kogen.Build.Report.build` and `Kogen.Build.Contract.verdict` through `test/kogen/two_outer_resumptions_test.exs`, and `Kogen.Codex.Compatibility.prepare_fixture` through `test/kogen/codex_compatibility_preparation_test.exs`. Main's controller renders the Candidate's `priv/kogen/prompts/developer.md` at every Developer launch and outer resumption of this Build, and `priv/kogen/prompts/reviewer.md` at every Review. So the Candidate's prompts keep every placeholder main substitutes, describe verification truthfully for both routes (Stop settles when a v1 context is supplied, the controller otherwise), and request a verdict that main's `Kogen.Build.Contract.verdict/4` still accepts when no ledger is supplied. Every edited cataloged test gets only its `source_sha256` refreshed in `priv/kogen/test-reliability.yaml` through `scripts/check/refresh_test_reliability_sources.py`. Declarations, dispositions, controls and consumer witnesses are unchanged. The consumer modules keep their witness text (for example `defmodule Kogen.Check do`), and `--check` reports nothing. The no-context check-and-block mode and the `KOGEN_TRACKING_CONTEXT` path are gone. The Bash PreToolUse gate guard is still registered in both harnesses and still blocks `make check` and every selected target. The Developer and Reviewer prompts and the README describe controller-owned verification. They mention the Stop scripts only as bootstrap remnants that the follow-up Intent deletes.
state.evidence: A rewritten stop_hook test drives both cases with a real git fixture and counting fake targets. Harness contract and core integrity tests assert the hook sets for both harnesses, and the verification_policy tests keep the guard's denial controls and assert that the new preflight no longer needs the Stop script. The existing reliability-catalog test validates the refreshed ledger. The three catalog rehearsals (selected by id, and run inside `check` by `scripts/check/rehearsals.exs`) fail when a trace identity is no longer observed, and a prompt-rendering assertion in the harness contract test renders both prompts with main's placeholder set.

state.given: A controller verification cycle in which targets pass, fail, or leave processes behind.

then_clauses.c0: Each receipt records the target, status, exit code, Candidate id, attempt token, context sha256, catalog sha256, cycle sequence, start and finish time, elapsed milliseconds, the output log path and sha256, and cleanup status.
then_clauses.c1: The controller runs each target in its own process group and, after exit, terminates any remaining group members.
then_clauses.c2: A target that leaves members that can't be reaped gets `cleanup: failed` and a failed receipt.
then_clauses.c3: Status comes from the exit code and cleanup only.
then_clauses.c4: A target-evidence manifest is snapshotted on pass *and* fail.
then_clauses.c5: Settlement rejects receipts with a mismatched binding, a rolled-back history or an altered log digest.

state.given: `verification_retries: 2` and a controller verification cycle that has failed.
state.when: The controller handles the failed cycle.

then_clauses.c0: The controller resumes the exact Developer session with `resume_build_developer`.
then_clauses.c1: The resume names the failed target and its receipt and log paths.
then_clauses.c2: It counts against `verification_retries` and never the outer allowance.
then_clauses.c3: The third consecutive failure since the last pass marks verification exhausted and stops the Build, before Jev and Review and ahead of other routing.
then_clauses.c4: A Review or unfinished-work outer resumption starts a new verification context, and its handoff needs a fresh controller pass.
then_clauses.c5: The superseded-objection rule from bounded-reviewer-evidence keeps working on controller cycles: a confident Developer objection in an attempt whose settled controller verification passed after an earlier controller cycle of the same attempt failed reaches the review packet as a labelled advisory.
then_clauses.c6: Every other confident objection still stops with `cannot_comply` as before.

scenario.given: The live Shape-to-Build fixture (`test/kogen/live_shape_to_build_test.exs`), whose nested Build may cite its own tracking record. Since bounded-reviewer-evidence, such a citation is stored as metadata plus an immutable sidecar at `.kogen/runtime/scenario-tracking/<build-id>/record-versions/<sha256>.json` (`Kogen.Build.Tracking.retain_record_version/2`), and cross-harness-adversarial-roles made `Kogen.Build.Evidence.resolve/2` verify every bound sidecar, found beside the resolved record (`record-versions/<sha256>.json`) or at its checkout-relative locator. That Intent fixed only the Reviewer-rework fixture (`Kogen.ReviewPacketAudit.preserve_record_versions!/2`, called from `test/support/live_reviewer_rework_fixture.ex`). At 363c20af the Shape fixture's private `preserve_tracking/3` still copies only `record.json`.
scenario.when: The live test retains the nested Build's evidence, deletes the fixture, and calls `Kogen.LiveReworkAudit.audit_retained!/1` on the retained copy.
scenario.then: A new support module `test/support/live_tracking_retention.ex` (`Kogen.LiveTrackingRetention.preserve!/3`) replaces the test's private `preserve_tracking/3`, and both of the test's retention call sites call it. For each nested Build it copies the whole `.kogen/runtime/scenario-tracking/<build-id>/` directory into `<log_dir>/scenario-tracking/<build-id>/`: `record.json`, its `record-versions/` sidecars, `review-packets/`, and the controller verification directory this Intent writes there (receipts, logs, ledger diffs). It rewrites each `build-summary*.json` `full_record.path` to the retained record, as today. After the fixture is deleted, `Evidence.resolve/2` of the retained summary succeeds. A missing or altered retained sidecar still fails resolution with "sidecar unavailable" or "sidecar mismatch". `Evidence.resolve/2` itself is unchanged.
scenario.wrong_result: Only `record.json` is copied, so a nested Build that cited its record fails the retained-evidence audit after cleanup (the failure of Build o-DlRi_iHnqIwmxfcCz-obe0 in the Reviewer-rework fixture); the live test keeps its own copy loop beside the new module; resolution is weakened to skip missing sidecars
scenario.evidence: A focused offline case in build_evidence_test builds a synthetic fixture whose record cites itself (a real sidecar written by `Tracking.retain_record_version/2`) plus a `build-summary.json`, runs `Kogen.LiveTrackingRetention.preserve!/3`, deletes the fixture, and asserts `LiveReworkAudit.audit_retained!/1` returns `:ok`. Two controls follow: a retained sidecar deleted (raises, "sidecar unavailable"), and one altered (raises, "sidecar mismatch"). The same case asserts that `test/kogen/live_shape_to_build_test.exs` no longer defines `preserve_tracking` and calls `Kogen.LiveTrackingRetention.preserve!`. The paid run retains the real nested Build's tree and resolves it after cleanup.

proof.paid_reason: provider-required: live-shape-to-build; observation: the retained tree of a real nested Shape-to-Build run, including any record-version sidecars its real roles produced, resolves after the fixture is deleted; offline-limit: whether a real run cites its record is model behaviour, so the synthetic offline case carries the sidecar controls

outcomes.o0: **One verification authority, removed in two steps.** After each Developer turn ends, the parent Build controller (the trusted code the Build started with, never code loaded from the Candidate) computes the Candidate identity itself. It runs `make check` and the selected targets as child processes outside the Developer process tree, and writes the only context, state and history. It never gives a Developer-launched process a verification context. For every Build started under this controller, that is the only writer. **Bootstrap:** this Build starts under main's controller, which can settle only from Stop-written state. So `check.sh`/`stop_runner.py` and their Stop registrations stay for exactly one commit, reduced to a single path. They run only when an older controller supplies a v1 unified `KOGEN_VERIFICATION_CONTEXT`; otherwise they print `{"continue":true}` and do nothing. The no-context mode, which runs `check` and blocks, and the `KOGEN_TRACKING_CONTEXT` path are deleted. A follow-up Intent built under the new controller deletes the Stop scripts and registrations. That follow-up is its own small verification Intent, not yet shaped. It is not `cross-harness-adversarial-roles`. The new controller also explicitly removes `KOGEN_VERIFICATION_CONTEXT` and `KOGEN_TRACKING_CONTEXT` from every child environment, because main's Stop runner passes its context down to any nested fixture Build. This Build must itself reach automatic verification, Review and commit; a manual finish is not accepted. The PreToolUse gate guard stays. The new controller also becomes the only writer of the local Verification Record and its history (`Kogen.Check`), so existing readers such as the `live-reviewer-rework` audit keep working unedited. The Candidate's preflight stops requiring the Stop script, so the follow-up can delete it.
outcomes.o1: **Failed verification resumes the same Developer.** A failed cycle resumes the exact Developer session through the existing `resume_build_developer`. The resume names the failed target and its retained receipt and log paths, and it counts against `verification_retries`, never the outer allowance. Exhaustion stops the Build with the existing precedence. Every outer resumption still needs fresh controller verification before handoff or Review.
outcomes.o2: **Candidate-bound per-target receipts.** Each receipt records the target, status, exit code, Candidate id, attempt token, context digest, catalog digest, cycle, start and finish times, elapsed time, the output log path and digest, and the cleanup outcome. It also snapshots any target-evidence manifest, as today.
outcomes.o3: **Rerun only failed paid targets.** Within one verification context (one outer attempt), a later cycle always runs `check` fresh. It reuses a paid target's earlier *passed* receipt only when the Candidate id and catalog digest are byte-identical, and marks it as reused with the cycle it came from. Then it runs the failed target and any target not yet run, in catalog order. Any Candidate change reruns everything. A new outer attempt reuses nothing.
outcomes.o4: **This Build leaves the target catalog and Makefile unchanged.** Main's controller stops any Build whose `priv/kogen/verification_targets.yaml` changed after admission, so this Build can't use outcome 8 on itself. `live-native` stays as it is. The follow-up verification Intent then uses outcome 8 to split it, under this Intent's controller.
outcomes.o5: **Provider policy stays inside the target that owns it.** Kogen core has no provider-timeout config, provider classification or provider retry. The Codex compatibility owner drops its Stop-hook portion, which depended on the no-context Stop mode deleted here. Its turn budget and one fresh-fixture timeout retry are delivered first by `cross-harness-adversarial-roles`, and this Intent leaves them unchanged.
outcomes.o6: **No target is special by name** (scenario `no-special-gate-target`). `mix kogen.build` no longer requires `make check`. `verified_by` is the complete, explicit list of targets a scenario needs. It must contain at least one offline target and at most one paid target, together with their dependencies. The Build runs exactly the union of those lists. Offline targets run fresh every cycle. Receipts are one uniform list. Make stays the only runner.
outcomes.o7: **Verification can't be quietly weakened, and the Developer can still change tests and targets freely.** Freezing definitions is false comfort, because `make ci` can call a `mix ci` alias that the Developer then empties. Instead, trust comes only from the admission commit, the admission catalog, the approved Intent and controller code: - **Targets** (scenario `same-intent-catalog-change`): the catalog is no longer byte-frozen. An Intent may add targets and select them (`catalog_changes.add`). Selected targets must exist in the Candidate. Anything else a Candidate changes in the catalog goes into the ledger. - **Proof tests** (scenario `controller-runs-proof-selectors`): the controller runs each scenario's proof tests itself. For new behaviour (`proof.base: fail`), those tests must also fail on the admission commit, with base's own runner and only the Candidate's test files overlaid. That catches empty, `assert true`, skipped and `:live`-hidden proofs. For preservation (`proof.base: pass`), base's version of an edited test must still pass on the Candidate. - **Everything else** (scenario `verification-surface-ledger`): every changed test or runner file, including files outside `affected_paths`, goes to Review with its diff. The Reviewer must mark each one `justified` or `weakening`, and code enforces that. Review also gets a report of base's test suite run against the Candidate. `weakening` blocks and goes back to the Developer. Nothing goes to Jev. The integrity fields live in the admission catalog, which this Build can't change. So this Intent ships and tests the mechanism, and the follow-up Intent switches it on for Kogen. Existing contracts, including this one, keep validating and are labelled `unproven-on-base`.

scenarios.offline-first-target-selection: Kogen's shared Shaping prompt (`priv/kogen/prompts/shaping.md`) describes `verified_by` as the complete explicit list, with no implicit `check`. It says to select a provider-backed target only when the scenario claims a provider-only observable that offline proof can't establish. scenarios.self-hosting-two-step-guidance: Kogen's `README.md`, not the shared Shaping prompt, has a maintained section explaining that Kogen builds itself. A Build runs main's controller, the code loaded when `mix kogen.build` started, against a Candidate that is changing the same machinery. Removals therefore follow expand and contract, like a zero-downtime database migration. One Intent adds the new path, switches the new controller to it, and keeps the old path working for the running controller. The next Intent, built under the new controller, removes the old path. state.scenario_then: The parent controller, running the trusted code the Build started with, computes the Candidate id itself (a private-index git write-tree, refusing assume-unchanged and skip-worktree entries). It runs `make check`, then the selected targets in catalog order, as child processes outside the Developer process tree. It re-checks the Candidate id after each target; a mutation fails the cycle. It writes the only context, state and history files, and no Developer-launched process gets their paths or `KOGEN_VERIFICATION_CONTEXT`. It is also the only writer of the local Verification Record and its history (`Kogen.Check.record_path/0`, `Kogen.Check.history_path/0`). After each cycle it writes them in today's line format (candidate, status, target, exit_code, session_id, attempt_token, finished_at), and it archives and resets them only at each outer attempt, as today. The record's `target` field keeps the constant `check` as a format value for existing readers; it selects nothing. So the unedited live-reviewer-rework owner and its support files (`test/kogen/live_reviewer_rework_test.exs`, `test/support/live_reviewer_rework_fixture.ex`, `test/support/live_rework_audit.ex`) keep working, and this Intent leaves them byte-identical, because it doesn't run that target. This holds even when the controller itself inherited one: for example, a nested `mix kogen.build` started by a target under main's Stop runner inherits the outer v1 context. The new controller explicitly removes `KOGEN_VERIFICATION_CONTEXT` and `KOGEN_TRACKING_CONTEXT` from every Developer, Reviewer and target child environment. That way a nested fixture's Stop hook can't write to the outer Build's state. The Stop hook does nothing. Handoff, Jev and Review read only this controller settlement. A complete Build through the new controller shows a failed-then-passed controller verification across a resume of the same Developer session, followed by Review and commit.

non_goals.n0: Any change to `Makefile` or `priv/kogen/verification_targets.yaml`, and any change to `priv/kogen/test-reliability.yaml` other than the `source_sha256` refresh of edited cataloged tests through `scripts/check/refresh_test_reliability_sources.py`. That includes the native target split, removing `live-native`, and ledger `target` strings. These belong to the follow-up verification Intent.
non_goals.n1: Editing the `live-reviewer-rework` owner or its support files (`test/kogen/live_reviewer_rework_test.exs`, `test/support/live_reviewer_rework_fixture.ex`, `test/support/live_rework_audit.ex`). This Intent doesn't run that target.
non_goals.n2: Deleting the Stop scripts and registrations, and paid proof of the Stop-free Codex compatibility fixture through a narrow target (follow-up verification Intent).
non_goals.n3: Any target runner other than Make.
non_goals.n4: Freezing target definitions or transitive runner files. Permission stays in `may_change_guarded_paths`, and weakening is caught by the controller-run proof checks and the Review ledger.
non_goals.n5: A paid red-on-base run. Provider-backed added targets are proved through their rehearsal tests as file selectors.
non_goals.n6: Mutation testing, and switching integrity on for Kogen's own catalog (the follow-up Intent does that).
non_goals.n7: Controller-level per-target timeout or cancellation policy. Hung targets behave as they do today.
non_goals.n8: Generic provider preflight, per-turn progress diagnostics, and failure classes in Kogen core.
non_goals.n9: Reusing paid receipts across outer attempts or Builds.
non_goals.n10: Controller generation freezing (`drafts/bind-controller-generation`), candidate workspaces (`isolated-candidate-workspace`), process-tree shutdown on Build exit, cost accounting, offline failure aggregation, and failed-Build return to Shaping.
non_goals.n11: Editing any other Intent package, including `cross-harness-adversarial-roles`.
non_goals.n12: Changing Jev, Review, handoff-report or review-packet semantics (beyond listing reused receipts and adding the bounded ledger), model routing, the default route, or native launch flags.

For each nested Build it copies the whole `.kogen/runtime/scenario-tracking/<build-id>/` directory into `<log_dir>/scenario-tracking/<build-id>/`: `record.json`, its `record-versions/` sidecars, `review-packets/`, and the controller verification directory this Intent writes there (receipts, logs, ledger diffs). It rewrites each `build-summary*.json` `full_record.path` to the retained record, as today. After the fixture is deleted, `Evidence.resolve/2` of the retained summary succeeds. A missing or altered retained sidecar still fails resolution with "sidecar unavailable" or "sidecar mismatch". `Evidence.resolve/2` itself is unchanged.
state.evidence: A focused offline case in build_evidence_test builds a synthetic fixture whose record cites itself (a real sidecar written by `Tracking.retain_record_version/2`) plus a `build-summary.json`, runs `Kogen.LiveTrackingRetention.preserve!/3`, deletes the fixture, and asserts `LiveReworkAudit.audit_retained!/1` returns `:ok`. Two controls follow: a retained sidecar deleted (raises, "sidecar unavailable"), and one altered (raises, "sidecar mismatch"). The same case asserts that `test/kogen/live_shape_to_build_test.exs` no longer defines `preserve_tracking` and calls `Kogen.LiveTrackingRetention.preserve!`. The paid run retains the real nested Build's tree and resolves it after cleanup.

then_clauses.c7: An Intent that edits a live test's owner file selects that test's target in the same Intent, because an edited live test that never runs is unverified.
then_clauses.c8: Otherwise an Intent selects at most one paid target, unless the Shaper explicitly accepts more, with the reason recorded in `questions.md`.

state.scenario_then: Each receipt records the target, status, exit code, Candidate id, attempt token, context sha256, catalog sha256, cycle sequence, start and finish time, elapsed milliseconds, the output log path and sha256, and cleanup status. The controller runs each target in its own process group and, after exit, terminates any remaining group members. A target that leaves members that can't be reaped gets `cleanup: failed` and a failed receipt. Status comes from the exit code and cleanup only. A target-evidence manifest is snapshotted on pass *and* fail. Settlement rejects receipts with a mismatched binding, a rolled-back history or an altered log digest.

That includes the native target split, removing `live-native`, and ledger `target` strings. These belong to the follow-up verification Intent.

state.scenario_then: (a) It prints `{"continue":true}`, runs no Make target, and writes no verification record, state, history or log. (b) It behaves exactly as today's unified protocol, so the older controller can settle, review and commit this Build automatically. `Makefile` and `priv/kogen/verification_targets.yaml` stay byte-identical to main, because main's controller stops a Build whose catalog changed after admission. `live-native` stays in the catalog unchanged. The target split belongs to the follow-up verification Intent. Main's `VerificationPolicy.preflight` still finds `.codex/hooks/check.sh`, `.codex/hooks/verification_policy.py` and the PreToolUse registration. The Candidate's own preflight requires only `.codex/hooks/verification_policy.py` and the PreToolUse registration, so the follow-up can delete the Stop scripts under this Intent's controller. Main's frozen catalog still runs every rehearsal inside `check`, so each rehearsal still observes its catalog trace identities, including `Kogen.Build.Verification.initialize` and `Kogen.Build.Verification.settle` through `test/kogen/verification_ownership_lifecycle_test.exs`, `Kogen.Build.Report.build` and `Kogen.Build.Contract.verdict` through `test/kogen/two_outer_resumptions_test.exs`, and `Kogen.Codex.Compatibility.prepare_fixture` through `test/kogen/codex_compatibility_preparation_test.exs`. Main's controller renders the Candidate's `priv/kogen/prompts/developer.md` at every Developer launch and outer resumption of this Build, and `priv/kogen/prompts/reviewer.md` at every Review. So the Candidate's prompts keep every placeholder main substitutes, describe verification truthfully for both routes (Stop settles when a v1 context is supplied, the controller otherwise), and request a verdict that main's `Kogen.Build.Contract.verdict/4` still accepts when no ledger is supplied. Every edited cataloged test gets only its `source_sha256` refreshed in `priv/kogen/test-reliability.yaml` through `scripts/check/refresh_test_reliability_sources.py`. Declarations, dispositions, controls and consumer witnesses are unchanged. The consumer modules keep their witness text (for example `defmodule Kogen.Check do`), and `--check` reports nothing. The no-context check-and-block mode and the `KOGEN_TRACKING_CONTEXT` path are gone. The Bash PreToolUse gate guard is still registered in both harnesses and still blocks `make check` and every selected target. The Developer and Reviewer prompts and the README describe controller-owned verification. They mention the Stop scripts only as bootstrap remnants that the follow-up Intent deletes.

state.given: An approved Intent whose `intent.yaml` declares `catalog_changes.add` with new target names. Its guarded paths cover the Makefile and catalog, and a scenario selects one added target. (This is a later Intent, or a fixture Intent in this Intent's tests, built under this Intent's controller. This Build itself changes neither the Makefile nor the catalog, because main's controller byte-freezes the catalog.)
state.when: The Build admits the Intent, and the controller verifies each Developer turn.

then_clauses.c0: The catalog is no longer byte-frozen after admission.
then_clauses.c1: At admission, `verified_by` may name a declared added target.
then_clauses.c2: It is rejected when it names an undeclared unknown target, or when `add` names a target that already exists.
then_clauses.c3: Each cycle, the controller reads the Candidate's catalog and Makefile only as data; it never loads Candidate code.
then_clauses.c4: Every selected target must exist in both.
then_clauses.c5: Every added target must meet every catalog rule (unique rank, dependencies, owner, and a rehearsal when provider-backed).
then_clauses.c6: A scenario that selects an added provider-backed target lists that target's rehearsal test as a file selector, so `controller-runs-proof-selectors` covers it.
then_clauses.c7: Removing, renaming or editing unselected targets needs no declaration; it appears in the verification-surface ledger.
then_clauses.c8: A missing or invalid selected target is a verification failure that resumes the same Developer.

state.scenario_then: No target name is special; Make stays the only runner. Admission no longer requires a `check` target. The plan loader accepts a scenario's `verified_by` when all of these hold: it is a nonempty list of distinct catalog targets; it contains at least one `provider_backed: false` target and at most one `provider_backed: true` target, which must equal `proof.paid_target`; every listed target's `dependencies` are also listed; and the list follows catalog rank order. The Build runs exactly the union of the approved `verified_by` lists, in rank order, and never silently adds a target. Receipts form one uniform list, with no separate `check` field in the tracking record, handoff report or review packet. The Bash gate guard blocks `make <goal>` for every catalog target, not a hardcoded `check`/`live` pair. The catalog validator requires at least one offline target with no dependencies, instead of `check`. This repository's existing contracts (`[check]` and `[check, <paid>]`, including this Intent's own) still validate unchanged. Maintained prompts and docs describe `verified_by` as the complete, explicit list.

state.scenario_then: The catalog is no longer byte-frozen after admission. At admission, `verified_by` may name a declared added target. It is rejected when it names an undeclared unknown target, or when `add` names a target that already exists. Each cycle, the controller reads the Candidate's catalog and Makefile only as data; it never loads Candidate code. Every selected target must exist in both. Every added target must meet every catalog rule (unique rank, dependencies, owner, and a rehearsal when provider-backed). A scenario that selects an added provider-backed target lists that target's rehearsal test as a file selector, so `controller-runs-proof-selectors` covers it. Removing, renaming or editing unselected targets needs no declaration; it appears in the verification-surface ledger. A missing or invalid selected target is a verification failure that resumes the same Developer. It doesn't stop the Build. The trust anchor for each rule is the admission catalog, never the Candidate's.

state.scenario_then: After the targets pass, the controller itself runs each scenario's file selectors on the Candidate, using the admission `focused_runner`. A failure is a verification failure through the normal retry path. This replaces the existence-only check (`verification_plan.ex:94-103`). For `base: fail`, it also runs them against the base. At admission it builds a controller-owned workspace outside the repository: `git archive` of the admission commit plus copies of `base_cache`. It records the workspace's digest and re-checks it before each use; on a mismatch it rebuilds the workspace. The catalog loader rejects a `base_cache` entry inside the controller's volatile state (`.kogen/runtime`, `.kogen/build.lock`, `.kogen/codex`, `.codex/sessions`), so the base workspace never inherits the running Build's lock or runtime. Every focused run there uses the workspace's own `MIX_BUILD_PATH` and resolves `priv/` and prompts inside the workspace, never from the parent checkout or the controller's application directory. Each cycle it overlays only the Candidate's bytes for that scenario's selector files and changed test-class files, never runner-class or implementation files. It runs the admission `focused_runner` there with a time limit. The run must exit nonzero. Exit zero fails verification as "proof cannot detect the change". A timeout or infrastructure error is an error, never a red result. The red receipt records the base commit, overlay digest, exit code, log path and digest, and a `red_kind` label (`assertion` or `load`). It is reused while the overlay digest is unchanged. For `base: pass`, a selector that differs from base becomes a ledger item. The controller also runs base's bytes of that selector on the Candidate, and they must pass there. A contract without `proof.base` still validates. Its base checks are skipped, and the report labels it `unproven-on-base`. A catalog without the integrity fields labels every scenario `integrity-not-configured`. Non-file selectors (rehearsal ids, root `.txt` fixtures, `scripts/check` files) stay existence-checked, and are labelled as such.

That includes the native target split, removing `live-native`, and ledger `target` strings. These belong to the follow-up verification Intent.

state.scenario_then: The controller computes a ledger from git (Candidate against base). For every changed surface path it records the status, the full diff and whether it is runner-class. It marks every target receipt that ran with changed runner-class files, and includes the catalog digest change. Added test-class files are left out; added runner-class files are included. The ledger goes into the handoff report and the review packet from bounded-reviewer-evidence, never to Jev. Each item's full diff is a controller-retained file under the attempt's verification directory. The packet carries one complete index entry per item (path, status, runner-class flag, diff stat, base and Candidate blob ids), plus a locator and sha256 for its full diff. It stays within the packet's 65,536-byte bound, and it never inlines a diff that would exceed it. The controller also runs base's test suite against the Candidate's implementation. Base's test files and runner go into the base workspace, with only the Candidate's implementation (non-surface) files overlaid. The result goes to Review as a packet summary with a log locator, a report and not a gate. The Reviewer must return exactly one disposition per ledger item, `justified: <scenario-id or finding-id>` or `weakening`, in a new `ledger` verdict field, kept separate from the existing finding `dispositions`. The field is required exactly when the packet carries a nonempty ledger. Without a ledger (for example when main's controller reviews this Build with the Candidate's `reviewer.md`), the verdict keeps today's exact keys. Both harnesses constrain the Reviewer's output with `Kogen.Harness.Verdict.schema/0` (Claude `--json-schema`, Codex `--output-schema`, both `additionalProperties: false`) and check exact keys in `Verdict.validate/1`. So the schema handed to a fresh Reviewer on either harness is chosen per launch: with a nonempty ledger it adds a required `ledger` array (one item per ledger path, `path` and `disposition`); without one it is byte-identical to today's schema. `Verdict.validate/1` and `Contract.verdict/4` accept `ledger` exactly when it was requested. A missing or extra disposition makes the Review malformed, through the existing malformed-verdict path. A `weakening` disposition opens a blocking finding that goes back to the same Developer as Review rework. If the Developer objects to the contract, the existing cannot-comply path returns the Intent to Shaping.

state.scenario_then: Kogen's `README.md`, not the shared Shaping prompt, has a maintained section explaining that Kogen builds itself. A Build runs main's controller, the code loaded when `mix kogen.build` started, against a Candidate that is changing the same machinery. Removals therefore follow expand and contract, like a zero-downtime database migration. One Intent adds the new path, switches the new controller to it, and keeps the old path working for the running controller. The next Intent, built under the new controller, removes the old path. The section lists, with source locations as of this commit, what the running controller reads or runs from the Candidate during a Build: the catalog and its change rules; the Make target definitions; the admission catalog's integrity fields; the files and registrations `VerificationPolicy.preflight` requires; the Stop scripts and registrations (bootstrap only); the guarded-path check; and the approved package. It gives this Intent and its follow-up verification Intent as the worked example: the Stop scripts are kept for the v1 context and removed next, and the `live-native` split is done next through declared catalog changes. It tells Shaping to check each Intent that touches these inputs, and to split it when one Build can't both change the input and still settle, review and commit.

state.scenario_then: A new support module `test/support/live_tracking_retention.ex` (`Kogen.LiveTrackingRetention.preserve!/3`) replaces the test's private `preserve_tracking/3`, and both of the test's retention call sites call it. For each nested Build it copies the whole `.kogen/runtime/scenario-tracking/<build-id>/` directory into `<log_dir>/scenario-tracking/<build-id>/`: `record.json`, its `record-versions/` sidecars, `review-packets/`, and the controller verification directory this Intent writes there (receipts, logs, ledger diffs). It rewrites each `build-summary*.json` `full_record.path` to the retained record, as today. After the fixture is deleted, `Evidence.resolve/2` of the retained summary succeeds. A missing or altered retained sidecar still fails resolution with "sidecar unavailable" or "sidecar mismatch". `Evidence.resolve/2` itself is unchanged.

non_goals.n0: Any change to `Makefile` or `priv/kogen/verification_targets.yaml`, and any change to `priv/kogen/test-reliability.yaml` other than the `source_sha256` refresh of edited cataloged tests through `scripts/check/refresh_test_reliability_sources.py`. That includes the native target split, removing `live-native`, and ledger `target` strings. These belong to the follow-up verification Intent.
non_goals.n1: Editing the `live-reviewer-rework` owner or its support files (`test/kogen/live_reviewer_rework_test.exs`, `test/support/live_reviewer_rework_fixture.ex`, `test/support/live_rework_audit.ex`). This Intent doesn't run that target.
non_goals.n2: Deleting the Stop scripts and registrations, and paid proof of the Stop-free Codex compatibility fixture through a narrow target (follow-up verification Intent).
non_goals.n3: Any target runner other than Make.
non_goals.n4: Freezing target definitions or transitive runner files. Permission stays in `may_change_guarded_paths`, and weakening is caught by the controller-run proof checks and the Review ledger.
non_goals.n5: A paid red-on-base run. Provider-backed added targets are proved through their rehearsal tests as file selectors.
non_goals.n6: Mutation testing, and switching integrity on for Kogen's own catalog (the follow-up Intent does that).
non_goals.n7: Controller-level per-target timeout or cancellation policy. Hung targets behave as they do today.
non_goals.n8: Generic provider preflight, per-turn progress diagnostics, and failure classes in Kogen core.
non_goals.n9: Reusing paid receipts across outer attempts or Builds.
non_goals.n10: Controller generation freezing (`drafts/bind-controller-generation`), candidate workspaces (`isolated-candidate-workspace`), process-tree shutdown on Build exit, cost accounting, offline failure aggregation, and failed-Build return to Shaping.
non_goals.n11: Editing any other Intent package, including `cross-harness-adversarial-roles`.
non_goals.n12: Changing Jev, Review, handoff-report or review-packet semantics (beyond listing reused receipts and adding the bounded ledger), model routing, the default route, or native launch flags.

state.given: An admission catalog that declares `verification_surface` (`tests` and `runner` globs), `focused_runner` (an argv template with `{paths}`) and `base_cache` (paths to copy). A contract whose scenarios carry the new `proof.base` field: `fail` for new or changed behaviour, `pass` for preservation.
state.when: The controller verifies each Developer turn.

then_clauses.c0: After the targets pass, the controller itself runs each scenario's file selectors on the Candidate, using the admission `focused_runner`.
then_clauses.c1: A failure is a verification failure through the normal retry path.
then_clauses.c2: For `base: fail`, it also runs them against the base.
then_clauses.c3: At admission it builds a controller-owned workspace outside the repository: `git archive` of the admission commit plus copies of `base_cache`.
then_clauses.c4: It records the workspace's digest and re-checks it before each use; on a mismatch it rebuilds the workspace.
then_clauses.c5: The catalog loader rejects a `base_cache` entry inside the controller's volatile state (`.kogen/runtime`, `.kogen/build.lock`, `.kogen/codex`, `.codex/sessions`), so the base workspace never inherits the running Build's lock or runtime.
then_clauses.c6: Every focused run there uses the workspace's own `MIX_BUILD_PATH` and resolves `priv/` and prompts inside the workspace, never from the parent checkout or the controller's application directory.
then_clauses.c7: Each cycle it overlays only the Candidate's bytes for that scenario's selector files and changed test-class files, never runner-class or implementation files.
then_clauses.c8: It runs the admission `focused_runner` there with a time limit.
then_clauses.c10: Exit zero fails verification as "proof cannot detect the change".
then_clauses.c11: A timeout or infrastructure error is an error, never a red result.
then_clauses.c12: The red receipt records the base commit, overlay digest, exit code, log path and digest, and a `red_kind` label (`assertion` or `load`).
then_clauses.c13: It is reused while the overlay digest is unchanged.
then_clauses.c14: For `base: pass`, a selector that differs from base becomes a ledger item.
then_clauses.c15: The controller also runs base's bytes of that selector on the Candidate, and they must pass there.
then_clauses.c17: Its base checks are skipped, and the report labels it `unproven-on-base`.
then_clauses.c18: A catalog without the integrity fields labels every scenario `integrity-not-configured`.
then_clauses.c19: Non-file selectors (rehearsal ids, root `.txt` fixtures, `scripts/check` files) stay existence-checked, and are labelled as such.

then_clauses.c0: The controller computes a ledger from git (Candidate against base).
then_clauses.c1: For every changed surface path it records the status, the full diff and whether it is runner-class.
then_clauses.c2: It marks every target receipt that ran with changed runner-class files, and includes the catalog digest change.
then_clauses.c3: Added test-class files are left out; added runner-class files are included.
then_clauses.c4: The ledger goes into the handoff report and the review packet from bounded-reviewer-evidence, never to Jev.
then_clauses.c5: Each item's full diff is a controller-retained file under the attempt's verification directory.
then_clauses.c6: The packet carries one complete index entry per item (path, status, runner-class flag, diff stat, base and Candidate blob ids), plus a locator and sha256 for its full diff.
then_clauses.c7: It stays within the packet's 65,536-byte bound, and it never inlines a diff that would exceed it.
then_clauses.c8: The controller also runs base's test suite against the Candidate's implementation.
then_clauses.c9: Base's test files and runner go into the base workspace, with only the Candidate's implementation (non-surface) files overlaid.
then_clauses.c10: The result goes to Review as a packet summary with a log locator, a report and not a gate.
then_clauses.c11: The Reviewer must return exactly one disposition per ledger item, `justified: <scenario-id or finding-id>` or `weakening`, in a new `ledger` verdict field, kept separate from the existing finding `dispositions`.
then_clauses.c12: The field is required exactly when the packet carries a nonempty ledger.
then_clauses.c13: Without a ledger (for example when main's controller reviews this Build with the Candidate's `reviewer.md`), the verdict keeps today's exact keys.
then_clauses.c14: Both harnesses constrain the Reviewer's output with `Kogen.Harness.Verdict.schema/0` (Claude `--json-schema`, Codex `--output-schema`, both `additionalProperties: false`) and check exact keys in `Verdict.validate/1`.
then_clauses.c15: So the schema handed to a fresh Reviewer on either harness is chosen per launch: with a nonempty ledger it adds a required `ledger` array (one item per ledger path, `path` and `disposition`); without one it is byte-identical to today's schema.
then_clauses.c16: `Verdict.validate/1` and `Contract.verdict/4` accept `ledger` exactly when it was requested.
then_clauses.c17: A missing or extra disposition makes the Review malformed, through the existing malformed-verdict path.
then_clauses.c18: A `weakening` disposition opens a blocking finding that goes back to the same Developer as Review rework.
then_clauses.c19: If the Developer objects to the contract, the existing cannot-comply path returns the Intent to Shaping.
